Raise the score for: explicit reference to sibling answers or their authors ('This is a complimentary note to MichaelNgelo and Sherushe's answers', 'Essentially the same as TheSilverDoe's but much simplified', 'This second answer gives a shorter proof, more algebraic, which does not expand on your ideas', 'probably a variant of what Qiaochu Yuan had in mind', 'This case is already nicely considered in the answer from ErickWong', 'mesel's answer about why ... is very good', 'As shown in this post and in the accepted answer'); additive or alternative framing ('Another point of view towards', 'Also note that', 'More conceptually', 'I will provide a geometric proof', 'I still felt like a complete proof using graph theory might add something to this thread', 'As mentioned before', 'I know that you ask about non-graph approaches in particular'); and any completeness or alternative-route move. Lower the score when the post engages the raw question from scratch as though nothing had yet been said. 0 = wholly from scratch, no awareness of any other answer; 5 = a single additive connective with no named reference; 10 = the post is explicitly positioned as an addendum to identified existing answers. Score EXTENT of the presupposition only. Do NOT judge whether adding to the thread was warranted or whether the addition is valuable.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the answer is framed as a hint, prompt, suggestion, or incomplete pointer rather than a fully developed response. Judge the framing only; do not judge whether it is pedagogically good or mathematically sufficient.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the amount of explicit language presupposing, referring to, correcting, or supplementing other answers, comments, or an existing thread. Judge only visible textual evidence; do not infer whether the response is better for doing so.
items.Y_desc: Score the extent to which the answer explicitly quotes or evaluates the asker's specific work, formulations, or previous attempts (e.g., 'You got to here'). Do not judge if the evaluation is accurate.

items.X_name: Second-person auditing of the asker's own attempt
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for HOW DIRECTLY THE POST ADDRESSES THE INDIVIDUAL ASKER AND THEIR SPECIFIC WORK rather than a general future reader. Raise the score for: second-person pronouns aimed at the asker; explicit reference to the asker's own posted attempt, notation, diagram, matrices or arithmetic ('Your DFA looks good to me', 'You just made a little arithmetic mistake near the end', 'You mixed them up', 'You seem to be greatly confused', 'Your matrices A(n) are parts of the infinite matrix', 'If, as you did, w = e^{iz}', 'from your own remarks', 'As pointed out in the question'); localisation of an error to a specific line of the asker's work; and closing checks aimed at that person ('Does that make sense?'). Lower it for impersonal exposition addressed to anyone. 0 = no address to the asker at all; 5 = occasional second person but no engagement with their attempt; 10 = the whole post is a line-by-line audit of the asker's own working. Score EXTENT of asker-directed address only. Do NOT judge whether the diagnosis is helpful, courteous or correct.
items.Y_name: Presupposes or names sibling answers on this question
items.Y_desc: 0-10: how much the answer's language presupposes that other answers to the SAME question already exist, or explicitly references them (e.g. naming another answerer by username, saying 'this second answer', 'a complementary note to X and Y's answers', 'essentially the same as X's but simplified', referring back to 'this post' as already having covered related ground). 0 = the answer reads as if engaging the raw question from scratch with no awareness of other answers; 10 = the answer is explicitly framed as a response to, or addition alongside, specific other answers. Score only this presupposition/reference, not whether the comparison it draws is accurate or fair.

Raise the score for: bare or near-bare URLs standing in for the explanation ('http colon slash slash en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_projective_plane - Look at the first two pictures on the right'); pointers to other questions or threads on the site ('See for example How many subgroups of order n does D_n have?'); a bibliographic citation carrying the answer (a journal reference given as the whole reply, or a pasted review record with an identifier, reviewer name and full abstract); pasted output or transcripts of an external computational tool (session lines such as 'In[383]:= ... Out[383]=', or appeals to what 'Mathematica uses' or what 'Wolfram Alpha says'); and referrals to offline or unlocated material ('My colleague ... has written up some notes ... I don't have the URL handy, but you might find the notes if you do a little sniffing about'). 0 = wholly self-contained prose and derivation; 5 = self-contained argument with one supporting pointer; 10 = the post is essentially a pointer, a citation or a paste. Score EXTENT of external sourcing only. Do NOT judge whether the reference is apt, authoritative, sufficient or correctly attributed.

Lower the score for uneven human prose that jumps, digresses, or assumes shared context. 0 = idiosyncratic voice throughout; 5 = template-like in places; 10 = the template runs end to end. Score EXTENT of the visible register only. Do NOT judge whether the reasoning inside is correct, and do NOT try to decide who or what wrote the post - score the register as it appears.
